summary: Decorated Green Beret Bo Gritz lied his way into fame as the 'real Rambo', fueled the myth of live US POWs in Southeast Asia with botched fundraised raids, then ran with far-right parties and sold land to Idaho militia followers.

evidence.note: joins Green Berets and deploys to Vietnam in 1965; main span starts here
1966 mission to recover a spy plane black box in Cambodia, with prisoner executions
origins of the POW/MIA flag and myth, and how Gritz spread it
fundraising tour built on a fabricated story about a dead comrade
1982 raid into Laos ambushed; later attempts staged from Thailand end in arrests
his POW fantasies inspire Rambo II, Missing in Action and other films
Populist Party VP run with David Duke in 1988, presidential run in 1992
accusations of racism and his antisemitic writings
Almost Heaven militia community in Idaho, lawsuits over land titles
1998 collapse of Almost Heaven, divorce and suicide attempt; main span ends

notes: The hosts say Gritz was still alive at recording (Nov 2025), so lifespan end is null and the lifetime rule extends covered_span to 2025. Reviewer: please verify, I have a vague memory he may have died earlier; if so, set the real death year. The POW myth and failed raids take the most airtime, so conspiracy-theories was chosen as primary over fascism-far-right (the description's framing). Latin America command 1975-77 mentioned only briefly, so no country added.
